summary:
First we have collected the data of moon and Mars from the nasa and other resources that given by the nasa apps challenge and splitted the geographical data of earth into the grid format then compare that data with the data of the mars and the moon if that data matches then we have called that place as the analog place.
The novelty is that we will check which activity can be done on that place and those activities include rover movement, data collection, drilling, habitat establishment, atmospheric and surface processes, terrain, miniralogy, topographic features and others.
Once we select the location on the moon or on the mars it will show it's features and location on earth and the characteristics and what operation can be done there.
If any location miss a characteristic then it wouldn't be declared as not a analog place but before that we check does it suitable for any of the operations if any one of the operation can be done then it is called as the analog place and there we can test and simulate the operation before performing the actual operation.
If any new location is found on moon and Mars through the APIs we get that data and perform the checking on earth then we can find the analog place for that location also.
details:
Our project PLANETREX is a web application that helps find places on Earth that are similar to locations on the Moon and Mars. We use real data from NASA and other scientific sources and compare 8 domains like terrain, geology, temperature, water, and other environmental conditions. Our aim is to discover new Earth locations that can be useful for planetary research.

Our project helps researchers find new planetary analog locations on Earth. It can reduce research time, make scientific data easier to understand, and help in testing equipment and planning future space missions.

We want to make planetary research easier and more accessible. Our main goal is to help scientists discover new places on Earth that can be used for Moon and Mars research and future space exploration.

We used Python, JavaScript, HTML, CSS, and FastAPI to develop our project. For scientific data, we used NASA PDS, LRO, MOLA, ASTER, NASA POWER, and Macrostrat. We used GitHub for managing our code and Render for hosting our website. We developed it using laptops.

The main difference in our project is that we don't just show already-known planetary analog locations. We try to discover new places on Earth by comparing real scientific measurements with Moon and Mars data. We are also developing an 8-domain similarity system to show how closely the locations match.

We mainly focused on scientific accuracy, reliable NASA data, finding new locations, and making the website simple to use. We also considered data availability, comparison accuracy, and how our project can be improved in the future.
